headline: The Fed held and the AI spenders split: Microsoft beat and is up premarket while Alphabet is down about 10% on a search miss and $9.1 billion of cash burn; Q3 GDP came in hot at 3.4% and oil eased to about $113 on new Iran peace feelers.
summary: The dashboard is still on Oct 27 closes (prices_as_of 2026-10-27, refresh running), so every close below is the Oct 28 close from Massive, the price source of record. The Fed held at 3.75% to 4.00% with two dissents for a hike (Bloomberg, CNBC), the S&P 500 rose 0.28% to 7,743.98, and the 10 year ended near 5.04% (Investing.com, Moomoo). After the close Microsoft beat on 48% Azure growth while Alphabet missed on search and burned $9.1 billion of free cash; at 8am ET Nasdaq 100 futures were down about 1%, Alphabet about 11% and Microsoft up 1.6% to 2.7% (Reuters, CNBC, TradingKey, StockTitan). This morning Q3 GDP grew 3.4% against 3.2% expected and September PCE matched estimates at 3.6% headline and 3.1% core, which keeps a December hike in play (AP, FXStreet). Samsung posted record profit but fell 4.13% on no new shareholder payout, Brent slipped to $113.32 on renewed US and Iran outreach, and Marvell is reported in advanced talks to buy Lumentum (CNBC, Reuters). WST beat and raised but its Oct 28 close over 398.67 came on 1.41 times volume, so the swing is still 'weak, wait'.

regime.why: The AI money is still being spent: Alphabet kept its $195 to $205 billion 2026 capex plan and Microsoft guided $170 billion for calendar 2027, and memory makers say supply stays tight into 2028. But growth and inflation are both running hot with the 10 year above 5%, so the market now pays only for spenders that show cash returns. Oil eased on diplomacy, but the post midterm Iran risk has not gone away.

signals.title: Microsoft beat and Alphabet missed: the market now pays for AI spending only when the cash shows up
signals.since_yesterday: Both reported after the close: Microsoft beat on 48% Azure growth, Alphabet missed on search and burned $9.1 billion of free cash.
signals.what_happened: Microsoft's fiscal Q1 revenue rose 19% to $92.28 billion against $90.69 billion expected, adjusted EPS was $4.89 against $4.73, and Azure grew 48% to $33.2 billion (CNBC, company release). Capex and finance leases were $45.2 billion; it guided over $50 billion next quarter and $170 billion for calendar 2027, and fiscal Q2 revenue of $96 billion to $97.1 billion (CNBC). Alphabet's revenue was $127.6 billion against $128.2 billion expected, adjusted EPS $2.67 against $3.02, and ad revenue $82.0 billion against $83.4 billion; Google Cloud more than doubled to $30.71 billion with a $561 billion backlog, but free cash flow was negative $9.1 billion. It kept 2026 capex at $195 billion to $205 billion and said 2027 will rise significantly (Reuters). At 6:30am ET Alphabet was down 10.63% and Microsoft up 2.69% premarket (StockTitan). Regular session closes on Oct 28: MSFT 531.01 on 1.36 times its 50 day volume, GOOGL 324.89 (Massive). Software also sold off on its own reports: Fortinet was down 25.7% premarket and ServiceNow about 19% (Investing.com, TradingKey). Meta reported a week ago, on Oct 21.
signals.so_what: Follow the money: the spending did not slow. Alphabet still plans about $200 billion this year and more in 2027, and Microsoft's $170 billion 2027 plan is real money for chips, memory, power and builders. What changed is who investors reward. Microsoft shows the cloud revenue and cash to pay for it; Alphabet is borrowing against a search business that is starting to slow, which CNBC calls the first real sign that AI is eating into search. Second order: if more spenders get punished for cash burn, some may pace 2027 orders, which would hit the suppliers last. Oracle's 10.73% jump on Oct 28 after promising to turn cash flow positive in the second half of fiscal 2028 says the same thing (Reuters). What would make this wrong: Amazon tonight showing AWS growth that justifies heavier spending, which would put the focus back on demand.
signals.for_you: Swing: MSFT is the one to watch. Its swing entry is 533.42; a confirmed trigger needs a close above it on at least 31.7 million shares today (1.5 times its 50 day average of 21.1 million, Massive). An open over the entry is not enough. Long term: MSFT was 'Buy zone now' at 531.33 on Oct 27, but a 2% to 3% gap up puts it above its 422.85 to 525.45 zone and the 2% band; wait for a pullback rather than chase. GOOGL is Wait, already below its 330.68 to 352.10 zone before the drop; do not sell puts into a fresh 10% gap. No action on META (reported Oct 21).

signals.title: The Fed held with two hawkish dissents, then Q3 GDP came in hot at 3.4%
signals.since_yesterday: The decision is out: a hold at 3.75% to 4.00% with Cook and Hammack dissenting, and this morning GDP beat while PCE matched estimates.
signals.what_happened: The Fed held at 3.75% to 4.00% and said 'the accumulation of more information' will guide its next step; Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland's Beth Hammack dissented (CNBC, Bloomberg). Chair Warsh said the economy is 'pointing in the right direction' and gave no guidance (Reuters). The Fed also said that in 2027 one of its eight meetings will carry no rate vote, leaving six chances to move rates outside emergencies (CNBC). The 10 year rose 4.3 basis points to 5.036% (Moomoo). This morning Q3 GDP grew at a 3.4% annual pace against 3.2% expected (AP), and September PCE rose 3.6% from a year ago with core at 3.1%, both in line; month over month they rose 0.5% and 0.3% (FXStreet).
signals.so_what: Growth near 3.4% with core inflation at 3.1% and rising is the mix that keeps a December hike alive. Two dissents for a hike tell you which way the committee leans. Fewer rate meetings next year means bigger moves when they come. Second order: rates above 5% raise the bar for every AI spender that is burning cash, which is exactly what punished Alphabet overnight. What would make this wrong: a sharp drop in jobs in the next payroll report.
signals.for_you: Puts: the 10 year at 5.036% is the bar any put premium must beat on an annual basis. Swing: no change; the data came in near forecasts, so the bigger driver today is earnings. Long term: higher for longer favors cash rich names like MSFT and JPM over heavy borrowers.

signals.title: Samsung's record quarter met estimates but the shares fell 4%: the memory chain now trades on payouts, not profits
signals.since_yesterday: Samsung reported: record profit roughly in line, HBM sold out for next year, but no new shareholder return plan until January.
signals.what_happened: Samsung's Q3 revenue was 195.25 trillion won against 195.79 trillion expected and operating profit 107.44 trillion won, about in line (CNBC lists the estimate as 106.66 trillion in one place and 107.66 trillion in another). The chip division earned 106.5 trillion won (CNBC). Samsung said its HBM is sold out for next year, the chip market stays tight through 2028, and chip capex rises 62% (Reuters). HBM4 reached 60% of its HBM sales (earnings call via Investing.com). It paid 30 trillion won of Q3 dividends but pushed its next return decision to January, and the stock closed down 4.13% while SK hynix rose 2.22% and the KOSPI fell 1.24% to 5,937.66 (CNBC, TradingKey). In New York on Oct 28, MU closed at 983.23, up 5.86% on 1.19 times its 50 day volume, and the SK hynix ADR (SKHY) at 164.70, up 13.3% (Massive).
signals.so_what: Two of the three memory makers now say supply stays short into 2028 to 2030, so pricing power holds. But when profits are this high and fully expected, the stock moves on what the company gives back. SK hynix promised about 100 trillion won; Samsung made investors wait. A 62% jump in Samsung chip capex is also the seed of the next glut, around 2028. For US accounts the memory story runs through MU. What would make this wrong: a hyperscaler cutting 2027 capex, which nobody did this week.
signals.for_you: Swing: MU's 5.86% gain came on only 1.19 times normal volume and it sits below its 20 day high of 1,108, so it is not a breakout; the dashboard still shows 'Not enough data' for MU. No chase. Long term: no change.

signals.title: Marvell is in advanced talks to buy Lumentum, and both are on the Buy zone list
signals.what_happened: Marvell is in advanced talks to buy data center optics maker Lumentum, with a deal possibly announced as soon as next week; neither company commented (Reuters, citing a source and Bloomberg News, Oct 28). Before the open MRVL was down over 11% and LITE up over 6% (TradingKey). On Oct 28, before the report, LITE closed at 913.95, up 5.52% on 1.28 times its 50 day volume, and MRVL at 251.65, up 3.32% (Massive). No price or terms are public.
signals.so_what: Optics is a chokepoint in AI clusters: every new GPU rack needs more lasers and transceivers, and Lumentum makes the lasers. A chip designer buying a laser maker says the scarce part is moving from the chip to the light that connects chips. Who pays: Marvell holders, through stock or new debt, which is why MRVL is falling. Who gets paid: LITE holders get a takeover premium, which caps its upside once a price is set. Third order: rivals that buy Lumentum lasers, like Coherent customers, may look for other suppliers. What would make this wrong: talks collapse, which would reverse both moves.
signals.for_you: Long term: both were 'Buy zone now' on Oct 27 closes (MRVL zone 218.02 to 250.63, LITE 769.18 to 948.65). Do not buy either before terms are public. MRVL near 224 premarket would still sit in its zone, but a stock falling 11% on deal fear is not a calm entry. LITE becomes a buyout story with a capped upside. No puts on either until the deal is announced. Swing: none.

signals.title: Oil eased to about $113 on new US and Iran peace feelers; XOM and CVX report tomorrow as open trades
signals.since_yesterday: Brent settled up 1.3% at $115.32 on Oct 28, then fell to $113.32 Thursday after Vice President Vance reached out to Iran and Qatar offered a new plan.
signals.what_happened: Brent settled at $115.32 on Oct 28, up 1.3%, and WTI at $102.78 (The National). Thursday morning Brent fell 1.73% to $113.32 and WTI 2.06% to $100.66 after Vice President JD Vance reached out to Iranian Security Council chief Mohsen Rezaei and Qatari mediators put forward a new proposal; a senior Iranian official rejected the proposals, while Iran's foreign minister said Tehran stays open to diplomacy (CNBC). The risk of US action after the Nov 3 midterms is still cited (CNBC). Baker Hughes fell 7.36% on Oct 28 after a Q3 beat, as the Middle East conflict dented oilfield services demand (Seeking Alpha, Investing.com). Oct 28 closes: XOM 182.02 on 0.96 times its 50 day volume, CVX 229.20 on 0.75 times, COP 149.06 on 0.84 times, EOG 160.92 on 0.63 times (Massive).
signals.so_what: Oil now moves on headlines in both directions within a day, and the war premium shrinks whenever talks look alive. Producers have done well, but the money that rides a war premium can leave fast, as in 1990 (see the cycle card). The oil service drop shows the war is not good for every energy company: closed Gulf fields mean less service work. What would make this wrong: a strike after Nov 3, which would send Brent back above $116.
signals.for_you: Swing: XOM and CVX are open trades, never confirmed by her volume rule. On Oct 28 closes XOM is about 1.72R above its 169.99 entry and CVX about 1.41R above 218.23 (my calculation). Both report Oct 30 before the open, so the plan rule says take profits or tighten stops today rather than hold through. COP (stop 135.75) and EOG (stop 147.98) stay open on light volume. Puts: none.

signals.what_happened: West Pharmaceutical reported Q3 sales of $874.5 million, up 8.7%, and adjusted EPS of $2.66 against $2.20 expected, and raised 2026 guidance to $3.41 billion to $3.42 billion of sales and $9.38 to $9.48 of adjusted EPS, from $3.345 billion to $3.38 billion and $8.85 to $9.05 (StockStory, RTTNews). Proprietary products sales rose to $728.8 million from $647.5 million; it bought back $685.3 million of stock in nine months (company release). Shares were up about 2% to 2.5% premarket (RTTNews, StockStory). Lilly's Q3 revenue rose 39% to $24.4 billion, driven by Mounjaro and Zepbound, and it raised 2026 revenue guidance to $91 billion to $92 billion from $85 billion to $87 billion; EPS guidance fell to $35.00 to $36.00 only because of $4.57 of acquired research charges (company release, Quartz); the stock was up over 5% premarket (TradingKey). On Oct 28 BLCO closed at 20.40, up 15.78% on 8.93 times its 50 day volume, after its Q3 beat and raise, and Boston Scientific fell 5.84% (Massive, Investing.com).
signals.so_what: Follow the money in GLP-1: Lilly's revenue jumped 39% on two drugs, and every injection pen needs West's plungers, seals and components, which is why WST's proprietary products grew 12.6% (my calculation). WST is the toll collector on the obesity boom and on biologics in general. BLCO is different: an 8.93 times volume day is real accumulation by funds, but the company still carries heavy debt. BSX slipping again shows medtech is splitting between growers and slow growers. What would make this wrong for WST: a slowdown in GLP-1 pen volumes as oral pills like orforglipron take share.

Today it confirms only with a close above 398.67 on at least 838,900 shares (1.5 times its 559,251 average). Long term: WST is Wait, far above its 210.80 to 285.20 zone. signals.title: Insider cluster buy in an AI chokepoint: TTM's CEO and a director bought a week after a 28% crash
signals.what_happened: TTM Technologies CEO Edwin Roks bought $440,350 at $88.07 and director Wajid Ali bought $902,461 at $90.25, both on Oct 28 and filed the same day (SEC Form 4 via the dashboard). TTM makes circuit boards for AI servers and defense and sits on the AI compute map. The stock fell 27.67% to 73.89 on Oct 22 on 7.02 times normal volume after its Q3 report, as its Q4 outlook disappointed and debt rose to fund the roughly $1.1 billion Epiq Solutions purchase (OCBJ, Massive). It has since rebounded to 90.79 on Oct 28, up 4.6% on 1.39 times volume (Massive).
signals.so_what: Insider cluster buys have the strongest research behind them, and a CEO buying into a crash says management thinks the sell off overshot. The money trail fits: every AI rack needs high layer count boards, and few US makers can build them for defense too. The risk is the debt: the buyers are betting the Epiq deal pays off before the interest bill bites. What would make this wrong: another guide down, or the stock losing the 73.89 low.
signals.for_you: Watch, not a trade. TTMI is Wait on the dashboard and below its 111.73 to 132.07 zone after a broken chart; the filing is one day old. A swing needs a base and a close over a pivot on 1.5 times volume first. This is the kind of setup to keep on a list.

Banks remain the weak link because a hike raises their funding costs and loan losses together. Farm credit is already tight, which hits machinery makers and the farm lenders. What would make this wrong: a credible spending plan from Lula's team before the Nov 3 to 4 decision.
signals.for_you: Long term: NU is Wait at 11.97, 8.6% under its 13.10 line (my calculation); no buy until it closes back over 13.10 and holds after the rate decision. cycle.quadrant_why: Q3 GDP grew at a 3.4% pace against 3.2% expected (AP), and September PCE rose 3.6% from a year ago with core at 3.1%, both up from August (FXStreet). Brent is still near $113 (CNBC).
cycle.short_term_debt_cycle: Tightening, late. The Fed held at 3.75% to 4.00% after September's hike, with two members voting to hike again (Bloomberg). The 10 year is at 5.036% (Moomoo).
cycle.long_term_debt_cycle: Late. The AI build is now partly funded with debt and negative cash flow: Alphabet burned $9.1 billion of free cash in the quarter (Reuters), and Oracle does not expect positive cash flow until the second half of fiscal 2028 (Reuters). Rates above 5% make that borrowing costlier.
cycle.big_cycle: External order: the US is mixing outreach to Iran with reported plans for action after Nov 3. Internal order: US midterms Nov 3. Technology: memory makers say supply is short into 2028 and beyond, and chip and optics companies are consolidating (Marvell and Lumentum).
tailwinds: Hyperscalers kept or raised capex plans for 2026 and 2027 (Alphabet, Microsoft).
Growth is strong at 3.4% and Lilly, WST and Microsoft beat and raised.
headwinds: A 10 year above 5% and a Fed leaning toward another hike.
Investors now punish AI spenders that burn cash (Alphabet down about 10%).

history.when: June 1999 to May 2000, Fed hikes into the tech capex boom
history.what: The Fed raised its target from 4.75% to 6.50% in six steps while companies spent heavily on internet and telecom gear (Federal Reserve rate history). The Nasdaq peaked in March 2000.
history.lesson: A Fed hiking into a spending boom does not stop it at once, but it changes who gets rewarded: first the market sells the spenders with weak cash flow, later the suppliers. Today's split between Microsoft and Alphabet is that first step.

history.when: July to October 1990, Iraq's invasion of Kuwait
history.what: Oil prices doubled from July to October 1990, then fell almost back to where they started within months once the outcome was clear.
history.lesson: War premiums vanish fast when diplomacy gains ground, as it did this morning. Take swing profits in oil names by plan, not by hope.

source.title: Are there useful lessons from the 1990-91 oil price shock? (The Energy Journal via JSTOR)

cycle.differences: In 1999 the spenders were young companies with little revenue; today they are the richest firms in the world, and Microsoft is paying with cash. But rates are higher now (5.04% on the 10 year) and the spending is far larger, so a slowdown in 2027 orders would hit suppliers harder.
